problem: Injecting physics-informed inductive biases into RL for wireless indoor navigation (WIN) requires heavy manual design (handcrafted states, architectures, rewards) and yields black-box policies. Purely symbolic (AoA-following) policies fail in multipath, high-order NLOS settings, and end-to-end RL is sample-inefficient and generalizes poorly.
motivation: Physics priors are easy for humans to state in natural language, so they should be equally easy to give to agents via a human-readable DSL. Some priors (reversibility) give executable policies, while others (max SNR at source, link-state monotonicity) only give desiderata, so RL is still needed to find a policy that satisfies them.
key_idea: Encode mmWave physics priors as RLang symbolic programs, where a meta-program either executes a symbolic policy (reverse AoA) or guides a PPO high-level waypoint policy through action restriction and importance-weighted cost correction.
insight: Both the symbolic and neural parts matter. Dropping the SNR-prior guidance raises 2+-NLOS NPL from 2.60 to 4.62, worse than the symbolic-only WAN (3.83). Dropping the link-state prior raises it to 3.90, and the agent frequently revisits high-order NLOS areas. Program guidance also shortens training: episodes per map fall and GPU hours drop by 26% on the first map and up to about 83% on later maps.
method: Neural perception: pretrained Neural SLAM (ResNet) yields map and pose estimate; low-rank tensor decomposition of mmWave measurements gives path tuples (SNR, AoA, AoD); an FC network estimates the link state (LOS / k-NLOS).
Physics priors in RLang: #1 reversibility (follow the strongest path's AoA), #2 SNR increases toward the transmitter, #3 link state decreases monotonically along an optimal path.
Symbolic policy 'reverse AoA': sets a waypoint 2.5 m along the strongest path's AoA and executes the visual-control Option.
Program-guided PPO (Neural Policy): outputs a waypoint angle from a discretized set (-170..180, 10° steps) given processed wireless features; reward is the distance cost to the waypoint.

ActionRestriction 'SNR prior': if SNR rose, only angles within ±10° of the movement direction are compliant; otherwise only the reverse direction. Non-compliant actions are replaced by a random compliant one, and the cost is importance-corrected as #compliant · π(a') · c (applied to the action loss only).
Link State Prior Effect: if the link state estimate increases, terminate the episode and restart.

Meta-program plus visual controller: uses reverse AoA if the link state estimate ≤2, else guided PPO. Fast Marching planning on the SLAM map gives short-term goals for a pretrained ResNet18+GRU controller (behavior cloning).

setting.backbone: PPO (GRU-based wireless encoder) as high-level neural policy + pretrained Neural SLAM (ResNet), FC link-state classifier, ResNet18+GRU visual controller (all pretrained modules frozen; only PPO trained); RLang symbolic meta-program
setting.training_data: PPO trained sequentially on 15 Gibson maps (A-O) x 10 target positions, 1000 episodes per task (early stopping when >6/10 successes); pretrained perception/controller modules from prior work
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + motion-sensor pose + processed mmWave measurements (angles, power, delays)
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN ±10°; high-level waypoint angle (36 discrete, 10° steps) from PPO
setting.simulator: Habitat with Gibson scenes (wireless signals simulated)
setting.privileged: none (transmitter location unknown; wireless measurements are part of the observation)

numbers_note: Non-standard benchmark (wireless indoor navigation on Gibson maps); the metric is normalized path length (NPL, lower is better), not SR/SPL. Full per-map results for maps P-U are in the appendix table, and only Map P and the averaged ablation are listed here. Training-efficiency results (GPU hours) are also reported.
results: On six unseen Gibson maps, PiPRL reaches NPL of about 2.1-2.8 in 2+-NLOS versus about 3.6-4.0 for the symbolic WAN and about 4.4-5.1 for NPRL and V-SLAM; it matches or beats the baselines in LOS and 1-NLOS. Training GPU hours fall 26% on the first map and up to about 83% on later maps versus NPRL.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation (Gibson with simulated mmWave), with no real robot and no standard navigation benchmark, and a compact set of 6 test maps.
Priors and the meta-program (thresholds such as link state ≤2, D=2.5 m) are still written by hand for mmWave, and depend on pretrained SLAM, wireless and controller modules.
The paper provides no significance testing for the training-efficiency claims. Baseline NPRL uses a different training scheme (rotation) than PiPRL (sequential).
